newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-DE BILDE MAKES ALL THE DIFERENCE FOR PSV.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DE BILDE MAKES ALL THE DIFERENCE FOR PSV.

text.p: The arrival of combative Belgian forward Gilles De Bilde at PSV Eindhoven was one of the most significant days of the Dutch season.
Both PSV and Feyenoord Rotterdam, the leading title contenders, had wanted his signature. PSV won that skirmish and ultimately the championship.
"If Feyenoord had had de Bilde, then Feyenoord would have been champions," said Jim Calderwood, manager of Willem II Tilburg. the side PSV beat 3-1 on Sunday to clinch the title.
"Without De Bilde, there would have been no title," concluded the newspaper Algemeen Dagblad in similar vein.
And without De Bilde's "bad boy" antics, the player would almost certainly have stayed with Belgian side Andelecht.
"If it weren't for the notorious punch, De Bilde would naturally not have been playing for us," said PSV coach Dick Advocaat.

De Bilde was suspended for three months for punching Aalst's Krist Porte, breaking his eye socket and nose during a match in December. He spent a night in police cells after the incident and was later banned by the Belgian soccer union.

In Belgium, De Bilde has fallen from grace since being voted Belgian Player of the Year in 1994. He also faces trial for allegedly hitting two male nurses in 1995 when he was denied access to his father in hospital.
FIFA had said De Bilde would not be able to obtain a licence to play in the Netherlands until the suspension was over by which time the Dutch transfer period would have ended.

That was sufficient to deter Feyenoord. But PSV pressed on and persuaded the national ruling body that, because they had signed De Bilde before the transfer deadline on March 7, he was eligible to play when the suspension ended.

De Bilde made his debut for the Eindhoven side at the start of April. In two months and just over 10 hours of play for PSV he has scored seven goals, including one in a vital 2-0 win over last year's champions Ajax.
He has also brought vital energy back to what was a deflated side. Most importantly, since De Bilde's debut in a goalless draw PSV have won all their matches.
So far his disciplinary record has been exemplary.
De Bilde himself is clearly delighted with his move to PSV.

"I came straight to PSV during what was a difficult time for me -- into a team of quality. As I was looking for a sporting revival, I grasped the chance with both hands," he said on Sunday before gulping down a mouthful of champagne.
